scale.source: CLDR RBNF sk renders 10^9 as "jedna miliarda" and 10^12 as "jeden bilión": Slovak counts in the long scale.

group_mark.source: CLDR common/main/sk.xml (unicode-org/cldr c0b65ae), number symbols: the group symbol is U+00A0, a no-break space. Pravidlá slovenského pravopisu (2000), Písanie čísloviek: "jednotlivé skupiny sa oddeľujú medzerou, napr. 5 328, 28 565". No dot groups digits.

decimal_mark.source: CLDR common/main/sk.xml (unicode-org/cldr c0b65ae), number symbols: the decimal symbol is a comma.

space_groups.source: Pravidlá slovenského pravopisu (2000), Písanie čísloviek: "jednotlivé skupiny sa oddeľujú medzerou, napr. 5 328, 28 565".

plural_scale_needs_count.source: CLDR RBNF sk writes a plural scale word only after its count ("dve tisíce", 2000). A plural scale word with no count names an amount, not a number.

scale_noun_agrees.source: CLDR RBNF sk %spellout-cardinal-masculine renders 10^6, 2 x 10^6, 5 x 10^6 and 21 x 10^6 as "jeden milión", "dva milióny", "päť miliónov", "dvadsaťjeden miliónov": the scale noun takes the number and case its count governs. The scale words of this lexicon are scale_numeral entries whose plural flag carries that agreement.

joiner_tens_units.source: CLDR RBNF sk renders 21 as "dvadsaťjeden"; Pravidlá slovenského pravopisu (2000), Písanie čísloviek: "dvadsaťsedem": one word with no conjunction.

joiner_after_hundred.source: CLDR RBNF sk renders 345 as "tristo štyridsaťpäť"; Pravidlá slovenského pravopisu (2000), Písanie čísloviek: "sedemstodvadsať": no conjunction after the hundreds.

joiner_between_groups.source: CLDR RBNF sk renders 1001 as "tisíc jeden"; Pravidlá slovenského pravopisu (2000), Písanie čísloviek: "tisícpäť": no conjunction between groups.

joiner_before_round_hundred.source: CLDR RBNF sk renders 1100 as "tisíc sto" and 1500 as "tisíc päťsto": no joiner stands before a round hundred after the thousands.

comma_between_classes.source: CLDR RBNF sk writes no comma between two classes (1001, 1100 and 1500 in the joiner settings above). No source opened shows a comma between two classes of one number, so a comma ends a number.

joiner_before_last_group.source: CLDR RBNF sk renders 1001 as "tisíc jeden"; Pravidlá slovenského pravopisu (2000), Písanie čísloviek: "tisícpäť": no conjunction stands before the last group.

ordinal_style.source: Pravidlá slovenského pravopisu (2000), Písanie čísloviek: "stodvadsiaty štvrtý účastník": every word of a written-apart ordinal is ordinal.

compound_words.source: Pravidlá slovenského pravopisu (2000), Písanie čísloviek: "Dovedna sa píšu číslovky v základnom tvare, napr. pätnásť, dvadsaťsedem, stojeden, sedemstodvadsať, tisícpäť, sedemtisícdesať." A word that is a sequence of number words reads as its parts.

bare_noun_counts_one.source: Slovak has no article, so a singular collective or fraction noun alone counts one: a paraphrase, with no page quote.

decimal_fractions.source: CLDR RBNF sk reads the decimals after "čiarka" as a cardinal ("dva čiarka päť"); this lexicon has no read source for a power-of-ten fraction after a decimal marker.

joiner.source: "a" joins a half to a whole: a paraphrase, with no page quote.

decimal_marker.source: CLDR RBNF sk: "x.x: << čiarka >>;". Slovak also reads the whole part with celá, celé or celých, as Czech does (Internetová jazyková příručka (ÚJČ AV ČR), "Členění čísel, víceslovné číslovkové výrazy (typ 365, 2 582) a desetinná čísla": "dvě celé tři"): for Slovak this is a paraphrase, with no read source.

minus_idioms.source: This lexicon lists no Slovak idiom that puts "mínus" before a positive number.

article_one.source: Slovak has no article; "jeden" is a numeral.

of.source: Slovak marks the counted noun by case, with no "of" word.

fraction_of.source: Slovak marks the counted noun by case, with no "of" word.

denominator_particle.source: Slovak has no particle like Portuguese "avos".

class_noun.source: Slovak names no digit class with a singular noun after a collective.

half_unit.source: The half "pol" is its own word before the unit, read by the half role: a paraphrase, with no page quote.

abbreviation.source: No Slovak number word in this lexicon is also an abbreviation with a period.

lone_decimal_mark.source: CLDR common/main/sk.xml (unicode-org/cldr c0b65ae): the decimal symbol is a comma; a comma before the first digit marks decimals.
